name: Crash sensitivity: long the quintile with the highest lower-tail dependence with the market (Chabi-Yo-Ruenzi-Weigert)
rule: meta: universe 'US_STOCKS_WIDE' (do not also set meta.assets), rebalance monthly, rank() mode. A name is eligible only if universe[sym].length > 505. Weights are equal-weight 1/N over the chosen names (N >= 3 else hold cash that period); sum <= 1. EW market = equal-weight mean of the daily close-to-close returns of every eligible name on each day (built from universe bars up to t only). Percentile cuts use the eligible cross-section at t (ties broken by symbol order). Over the last 504 sessions: q_i = the 5th percentile of r_i, q_m = the 5th percentile of the EW market m (both over the same window, linear interpolation). LTD_i = (# days with r_i <= q_i AND m <= q_m) / (# days with m <= q_m). Names whose window is incomplete are ineligible. Long the top 20% by LTD, equal weight. Overseer fix: meta.warmup = 526 (first rebalance after names reach 505 bars), so the deterministic cash warm-up is scored for neither the rule nor B&H.
rationale: Investors demand compensation for stocks that crash exactly when the market crashes; the paper finds a crash-sensitivity premium that survives controls for beta, downside beta and coskewness, so a price-only tail-dependence sort is a direct test.
source: Chabi-Yo, Ruenzi & Weigert 2018, 'Crash sensitivity and the cross-section of expected stock returns', Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis 53(3), 1059-1100

name: Realized semibetas: long the quintile with the highest negative-minus-positive semibeta (Bollerslev-Patton-Quaedvlieg)
rule: meta: universe 'US_STOCKS_WIDE' (do not also set meta.assets), rebalance monthly, rank() mode. A name is eligible only if universe[sym].length > 70. Weights are equal-weight 1/N over the chosen names (N >= 3 else hold cash that period); sum <= 1. EW market = equal-weight mean of the daily close-to-close returns of every eligible name on each day (built from universe bars up to t only). Percentile cuts use the eligible cross-section at t (ties broken by symbol order). Over the last 63 sessions with m = EW market return and r_i the name's return: betaN_i = sum(min(r_i,0)*min(m,0)) / sum(m^2); betaP_i = sum(max(r_i,0)*max(m,0)) / sum(m^2). score_i = betaN_i - betaP_i. Long the top 20% by score, equal weight.
rationale: Decomposing beta by the signs of stock and market moves, the paper finds the negative semibeta (co-movement on market down days) carries a positive premium and the positive semibeta a negative one, so the spread should pick names that are paid for downside co-movement.
source: Bollerslev, Patton & Quaedvlieg 2022, 'Realized semibetas: disentangling 'good' and 'bad' downside risks', Journal of Financial Economics 144(1), 227-246

name: Salience theory: long the quintile with the lowest salience-weighted past-month return (Cosemans-Frehen)
rule: meta: universe 'US_STOCKS_WIDE' (do not also set meta.assets), rebalance monthly, rank() mode. A name is eligible only if universe[sym].length > 30. Weights are equal-weight 1/N over the chosen names (N >= 3 else hold cash that period); sum <= 1. EW market = equal-weight mean of the daily close-to-close returns of every eligible name on each day (built from universe bars up to t only). Percentile cuts use the eligible cross-section at t (ties broken by symbol order). Over the last 21 sessions (bars t-20..t): rbar_d = EW market return on day d; sal_i,d = |r_i,d - rbar_d| / (|r_i,d| + |rbar_d| + 0.1). For each name rank its 21 days by sal descending (k = 1 most salient); omega_k = 0.7^k / sum_{j=1..21} 0.7^j. ST_i = sum_d (omega_i,d - 1/21) * r_i,d (covariance between the salience weight and the return). Long the bottom 20% by ST (least salient upside / most salient downside), equal weight.
rationale: Under salience theory investors overweight a stock's most eye-catching past returns relative to the market; stocks with salient upside get overpriced and earn low subsequent returns, and the paper reports a monotonic ST spread that is not explained by standard factors or short-term reversal.
source: Cosemans & Frehen 2021, 'Salience theory and stock prices: empirical evidence', Journal of Financial Economics 140(2), 460-483

name: Average skewness timing: hold the equity universe only when average cross-sectional skewness is below its historical median (Jondeau-Zhang-Zhu)
rule: meta: universe 'US_STOCKS_WIDE' (do not also set meta.assets), rebalance monthly, rank() mode. A name is eligible only if universe[sym].length > 30. Weights are equal-weight 1/N over the chosen names (N >= 3 else hold cash that period); sum <= 1. EW market = equal-weight mean of the daily close-to-close returns of every eligible name on each day (built from universe bars up to t only). Percentile cuts use the eligible cross-section at t (ties broken by symbol order). skew_i = sample skewness of the name's last 21 daily returns (sum((r-mean)^3)/21 divided by (sum((r-mean)^2)/21)^1.5). AS_t = equal-weight mean of skew_i across eligible names. Keep ctx.state.hist = every AS_t from earlier monthly rebalances (expanding, excluding t). If fewer than 24 entries: cash (still push). Else if AS_t <= median(ctx.state.hist): long every eligible name equal weight; else cash. Push AS_t after deciding. Overseer fix: meta.warmup = 535 (first decision after 24 monthly AS observations), so the deterministic cash warm-up is scored for neither the rule nor B&H.
rationale: Jondeau, Zhang and Zhu show the average skewness of individual stocks negatively predicts next-month market returns (high average skewness marks lottery-like optimism), with out-of-sample R-squared comparable to the best known predictors.
source: Jondeau, Zhang & Zhu 2019, 'Average skewness matters', Journal of Financial Economics 134(1), 29-47

name: Pre-holiday beta rotation: high-beta quintile on the session before each NYSE holiday, low-beta quintile otherwise (Ariel; Savor-Wilson shape)
rule: meta: universe 'US_STOCKS_WIDE' (do not also set meta.assets), rebalance daily, rank() mode. A name is eligible only if universe[sym].length > 260. Weights are equal-weight 1/N over the chosen names (N >= 3 else hold cash that period); sum <= 1. EW market = equal-weight mean of the daily close-to-close returns of every eligible name on each day (built from universe bars up to t only). Percentile cuts use the eligible cross-section at t (ties broken by symbol order). beta_i = cov(ret_i, EW market)/var(EW market) over the last 252 sessions. Dates: ymd(t) = UTC calendar date of bar.time (epoch seconds; US bars open at 00:00 UTC of the session date); dow(t) = (floor(t/86400)+4) % 7 with 0 = Sunday. nextSession(t) = the next weekday date after ymd(t) (Fri -> Mon); a holiday error there only shifts a boundary by one session. NYSE holidays (deterministic rules, observed on the nearest weekday when on a weekend): Jan 1; 3rd Monday Jan; 3rd Monday Feb; Good Friday (Easter via the Gregorian computus); last Monday May; Jun 19 (from 2022); Jul 4; 1st Monday Sep; 4th Thursday Nov; Dec 25. P = nextSession(t). If the first weekday after P is an NYSE holiday (so P is the pre-holiday session), long the top 20% by beta; otherwise long the bottom 20% by beta. Equal weight. Overseer fix: meta.warmup = 261 (names reach 260 bars), so the deterministic cash warm-up is scored for neither the rule nor B&H.
rationale: Ariel found a large share of the equity premium accrues on the sessions before exchange holidays; if it is a risk premium concentrated on specific days (as Savor-Wilson argue for announcement days), beta should be rewarded on those sessions and not otherwise.
source: Ariel 1990, 'High stock returns before holidays: existence and evidence on possible causes', Journal of Finance 45(5), 1611-1626; Savor & Wilson 2014, JFE 113(2)

name: Momentum in quarter-ending months: 12-1 winners held only in March, June, September and December (Sias)
rule: meta: universe 'US_STOCKS_WIDE' (do not also set meta.assets), rebalance monthly, rank() mode. A name is eligible only if universe[sym].length > 253. Weights are equal-weight 1/N over the chosen names (N >= 3 else hold cash that period); sum <= 1. EW market = equal-weight mean of the daily close-to-close returns of every eligible name on each day (built from universe bars up to t only). Percentile cuts use the eligible cross-section at t (ties broken by symbol order). Dates: ymd(t) = UTC calendar date of bar.time (epoch seconds; US bars open at 00:00 UTC of the session date); dow(t) = (floor(t/86400)+4) % 7 with 0 = Sunday. nextSession(t) = the next weekday date after ymd(t) (Fri -> Mon); a holiday error there only shifts a boundary by one session. mom_i = close[t-21]/close[t-252] - 1. The rebalance bar t is the last session of its calendar month; M = the calendar month of nextSession(t). If M is 3, 6, 9 or 12: long the top 20% by mom, equal weight; otherwise cash. Overseer fix: meta.warmup = 274 (first monthly rebalance after names reach 253 bars), so the deterministic cash warm-up is scored for neither the rule nor B&H.
rationale: Sias documents that momentum profits are concentrated in quarter-ending months and attributes it to institutional window dressing and quarter-end performance reporting, so a momentum sleeve run only in those months should capture most of the premium with a quarter of the exposure.
source: Sias 2007, 'Causes and seasonality of momentum profits', Financial Analysts Journal 63(2), 48-54

name: Prospect-theory value: long the quintile with the lowest TK value of the past 60 monthly returns (Barberis-Mukherjee-Wang)
rule: meta: universe 'US_STOCKS_WIDE' (do not also set meta.assets), rebalance monthly, rank() mode. A name is eligible only if universe[sym].length > 30. Weights are equal-weight 1/N over the chosen names (N >= 3 else hold cash that period); sum <= 1. EW market = equal-weight mean of the daily close-to-close returns of every eligible name on each day (built from universe bars up to t only). Percentile cuts use the eligible cross-section at t (ties broken by symbol order). Monthly returns from ctx.resample(universe[sym], '1M') using only complete months; a name is eligible only if it has at least 60 complete months, and the last 60 are used (L = 60). TK of a return list of length L: v(x) = x^0.88 for x >= 0 and -2.25*(-x)^0.88 for x < 0; w+(p) = p^0.61/(p^0.61+(1-p)^0.61)^(1/0.61); w-(p) = p^0.69/(p^0.69+(1-p)^0.69)^(1/0.69). Sort the m negative returns ascending r(-m) <= ... <= r(-1) and the n non-negative returns ascending r(1) <= ... <= r(n). TK = sum_{j=1..m} v(r(-j)) * [w-(j/L) - w-((j-1)/L)] + sum_{j=1..n} v(r(j)) * [w+((n-j+1)/L) - w+((n-j)/L)]. Long the bottom 20% by TK, equal weight. Overseer fix: meta.warmup = 1289 (union-calendar days before 2021-11-01, when names first have 60 complete months), so the deterministic cash warm-up is scored for neither the rule nor B&H.
rationale: Barberis, Mukherjee and Wang argue investors evaluate a stock by the prospect-theory value of its historical return distribution; high-TK stocks (positively skewed, big past gains) are overpriced and earn low returns, which they confirm across US and international markets.
source: Barberis, Mukherjee & Wang 2016, 'Prospect theory and stock returns: an empirical test', Review of Financial Studies 29(11), 3068-3107

name: Trend-following crisis alpha, fast: 1-month long-short vol-scaled TSMOM on 23 non-index ETFs only while QQQ is 10% off its 1-year high, QQQ/DIA otherwise (Hamill-Rattray-van Hemert)
rule: rank() mode, rebalance weekly, assets = the 25 discovery ETFs, longShort. Dates: ymd(t) = UTC calendar date of bar.time (epoch seconds; US bars open at 00:00 UTC of the session date); dow(t) = (floor(t/86400)+4) % 7 with 0 = Sunday. nextSession(t) = the next weekday date after ymd(t) (Fri -> Mon); a holiday error there only shifts a boundary by one session. Index drawdown: dd = QQQ close[t] / max(QQQ close over bars t-251..t) - 1 (QQQ needs > 252 bars). Non-crisis (dd > -0.10): weights QQQ 0.5, DIA 0.5. Crisis (dd <= -0.10): for each of the 23 non-index ETFs with > 84 bars, sgn_i = sign(close[t]/close[t-21] - 1) (0 -> no position), vol_i = std(last 63 daily returns)*sqrt(252), w_i = sgn_i * (0.10/23) / vol_i capped to |w_i| <= 0.15; if the gross sum |w| exceeds 1, scale all weights down proportionally. QQQ/DIA weight 0 in crisis. Overseer fix: if DIA has no bar at t return {} (cash; inside the warm-up). Crisis-book members are only the non-index ETFs present at t with > 84 bars; the divisor stays 23. Overseer fix: meta.warmup = 2950 (union-calendar days before 2016-09-21 (DIA and the 23 non-index ETFs start 2016-09-14; only QQQ/AGG/GLD exist before)), so the deterministic cash warm-up is scored for neither the rule nor B&H.
rationale: Hamill, Rattray and van Hemert show trend following earned its 'crisis alpha' in equity drawdowns mainly from faster signals that flip to short bonds-up/commodities-down trends within weeks; switching to a fast long-short trend book only inside a drawdown tests whether that hedge value exists in a 25-ETF universe.
source: Hamill, Rattray & van Hemert 2016, 'Trend following: equity and bond crisis alpha', Journal of Portfolio Management 42(5), 11-31; Hurst, Ooi & Pedersen 2017, JPM 44(1)

name: Trend-following crisis alpha, slow: 12-month long-short vol-scaled TSMOM on 23 non-index ETFs only while QQQ is 10% off its 1-year high (Hamill-Rattray-van Hemert, slow-signal variant)
rule: rank() mode, rebalance weekly, assets = the 25 discovery ETFs, longShort. Dates: ymd(t) = UTC calendar date of bar.time (epoch seconds; US bars open at 00:00 UTC of the session date); dow(t) = (floor(t/86400)+4) % 7 with 0 = Sunday. nextSession(t) = the next weekday date after ymd(t) (Fri -> Mon); a holiday error there only shifts a boundary by one session. Index drawdown: dd = QQQ close[t] / max(QQQ close over bars t-251..t) - 1 (QQQ needs > 252 bars). Non-crisis (dd > -0.10): weights QQQ 0.5, DIA 0.5. Crisis (dd <= -0.10): for each of the 23 non-index ETFs with > 315 bars, sgn_i = sign(close[t]/close[t-252] - 1) (0 -> no position), vol_i = std(last 63 daily returns)*sqrt(252), w_i = sgn_i * (0.10/23) / vol_i capped to |w_i| <= 0.15; if the gross sum |w| exceeds 1, scale all weights down proportionally. QQQ/DIA weight 0 in crisis. (Variant of c1023-acad2-11 with the 12-month lookback; the paper predicts weaker crisis alpha for slow signals.) Overseer fix: if DIA has no bar at t return {} (cash; inside the warm-up). Crisis-book members are only the non-index ETFs present at t with > 315 bars; the divisor stays 23. Overseer fix: meta.warmup = 2950 (same as c1023-acad2-11), so the deterministic cash warm-up is scored for neither the rule nor B&H.
rationale: Same crisis-alpha test with the standard 12-month trend signal; the paper's finding that slow signals react too late in fast sell-offs predicts this variant should do worse than the 1-month version, which makes the pair a direct test of the speed claim.
source: Hamill, Rattray & van Hemert 2016, 'Trend following: equity and bond crisis alpha', Journal of Portfolio Management 42(5), 11-31

name: Quarter-end rebalancing flows: tilt to the quarter's laggard (bonds vs stocks) over the last 3 sessions of each calendar quarter (Harvey-Mazzoleni-Melone)
rule: rank() mode, rebalance daily, assets QQQ DIA TLT IEF. Dates: ymd(t) = UTC calendar date of bar.time (epoch seconds; US bars open at 00:00 UTC of the session date); dow(t) = (floor(t/86400)+4) % 7 with 0 = Sunday. nextSession(t) = the next weekday date after ymd(t) (Fri -> Mon); a holiday error there only shifts a boundary by one session. r = number of weekdays strictly after ymd(t) and still inside the same calendar quarter. Window = (1 <= r <= 3), so bar i+1 is one of the last 3 sessions of the quarter. Q0 = the close of the last session of the previous calendar quarter (first bar whose ymd is in the current quarter minus one). eq = 0.5*(QQQ close[t]/QQQ Q0 + DIA close[t]/DIA Q0) - 1; bd = 0.5*(TLT close[t]/TLT Q0 + IEF close[t]/IEF Q0) - 1. Outside the window, or when |eq - bd| <= 0.03: weights 0.25 each (the neutral book). In the window with eq - bd > 0.03: TLT 0.5, IEF 0.5. In the window with eq - bd < -0.03: QQQ 0.5, DIA 0.5. Overseer fix: if DIA, TLT or IEF has no bar at t or at the Q0 bar, return {} (cash; inside the warm-up). Overseer fix: meta.warmup = 2958 (union-calendar days before 2016-10-01 (first full quarter with DIA/TLT/IEF)), so the deterministic cash warm-up is scored for neither the rule nor B&H.
rationale: Harvey, Mazzoleni and Melone show that calendar rebalancing by large stock-bond portfolios is predictable: after a quarter in which stocks beat bonds, rebalancers sell stocks and buy bonds into quarter-end (and vice versa), and the price impact is measurable in the last sessions of the quarter.
source: Harvey, Mazzoleni & Melone 2023, 'The unintended consequences of rebalancing', SSRN working paper 4379780; Etula, Rinne, Suominen & Vaittinen 2020, 'Dash for cash', RFS 33(1)

name: Cross-asset same-calendar-month seasonality: top 5 of 25 ETFs by their average return in the coming calendar month over prior years (Keloharju-Linnainmaa-Nyberg)
rule: rank() mode, rebalance monthly, assets = the 25 discovery ETFs. Dates: ymd(t) = UTC calendar date of bar.time (epoch seconds; US bars open at 00:00 UTC of the session date); dow(t) = (floor(t/86400)+4) % 7 with 0 = Sunday. nextSession(t) = the next weekday date after ymd(t) (Fri -> Mon); a holiday error there only shifts a boundary by one session. Monthly returns from ctx.resample(universe[sym], '1M') using only complete months. M = the calendar month of nextSession(t). score_i = mean of asset i's past returns in calendar month M over all prior years with a complete month M (eligible only if at least 3 such observations). Long the top 5 by score, equal weight (fewer if fewer than 5 eligible, min 3 else cash). Overseer fix: meta.warmup = 3711 (union-calendar days before 2019-10-01, when the 2016-09 ETFs first have 3 same-month observations), so the deterministic cash warm-up is scored for neither the rule nor B&H.
rationale: Keloharju, Linnainmaa and Nyberg show that an asset's past returns in the same calendar month predict its return in that month across stocks, commodities and country indices alike; the only tested versions here are stock-level and sector-level, not the multi-asset-class version the paper emphasises.
source: Keloharju, Linnainmaa & Nyberg 2016, 'Return seasonalities', Journal of Finance 71(4), 1557-1590; Heston & Sadka 2008, JFE 87(2)

name: Announcement-day Treasuries: long TLT/IEF only over employment-report and FOMC sessions (Savor-Wilson)
rule: signal() mode. Dates: ymd(t) = UTC calendar date of bar.time (epoch seconds; US bars open at 00:00 UTC of the session date); dow(t) = (floor(t/86400)+4) % 7 with 0 = Sunday. nextSession(t) = the next weekday date after ymd(t) (Fri -> Mon); a holiday error there only shifts a boundary by one session. Employment-report day R for calendar month M (BLS rule: the 3rd Friday after the Sun-Sat week containing the 12th): d12 = M-12; sat = d12 + (6 - dow(d12)) days; R = sat + 20 days (always a Friday). Build the set of all R for every month in the sample a priori. FOMC decision dates = the FOMC_DATES list in research/hunt2/strategies/calendar-fomc-drift.mjs copied verbatim into the module (regular meetings 2016-01-27 .. 2025-03-19; the unscheduled 2020-03-03 and 2020-03-15 entries are excluded). Return 1 at bar i if ymd(bars[i].time + 86400) is an employment-report day R or an FOMC decision date (position held from the prior close through the announcement session); else 0.
rationale: Savor and Wilson find that Treasury bonds, like stocks, earn a large share of their excess return on scheduled macro-announcement days as compensation for bearing the news risk; the prior tests covered equities only.
source: Savor & Wilson 2013, 'How much do investors care about macroeconomic risk? Evidence from scheduled economic announcements', JFQA 48(2), 343-375

name: Daylight-saving Monday: flat QQQ/DIA on the first session after each clock change, long otherwise (Kamstra-Kramer-Levi)
rule: signal() mode. Dates: ymd(t) = UTC calendar date of bar.time (epoch seconds; US bars open at 00:00 UTC of the session date); dow(t) = (floor(t/86400)+4) % 7 with 0 = Sunday. nextSession(t) = the next weekday date after ymd(t) (Fri -> Mon); a holiday error there only shifts a boundary by one session. US clock changes (rule since 2007): the second Sunday of March and the first Sunday of November. Return 0 at bar i if nextSession(t) is the Monday immediately following a clock-change Sunday; else 1. Overseer fix: before 2007 use the 1987-2006 US rule (clock changes on the first Sunday of April and the last Sunday of October); from 2007 the rule above.
rationale: Kamstra, Kramer and Levi report significantly negative returns on the first trading day after daylight-saving clock changes, attributing it to sleep disruption; it is one of the most-cited and most-disputed calendar anomalies and has not been tested here.
source: Kamstra, Kramer & Levi 2000, 'Losing sleep at the market: the daylight saving anomaly', American Economic Review 90(4), 1005-1011

name: Post-FOMC drift in Treasuries: hold TLT/IEF in the direction of the FOMC-day move for the next 15 sessions (Brooks-Katz-Lustig)
rule: signal() mode, longShort. Dates: ymd(t) = UTC calendar date of bar.time (epoch seconds; US bars open at 00:00 UTC of the session date); dow(t) = (floor(t/86400)+4) % 7 with 0 = Sunday. nextSession(t) = the next weekday date after ymd(t) (Fri -> Mon); a holiday error there only shifts a boundary by one session. FOMC decision dates = the FOMC_DATES list in research/hunt2/strategies/calendar-fomc-drift.mjs copied verbatim into the module (regular meetings 2016-01-27 .. 2025-03-19; the unscheduled 2020-03-03 and 2020-03-15 entries are excluded). Let F be the most recent FOMC date with ymd(bars[j].time) == F for some j <= i, and k = i - j (sessions since the FOMC bar; k = 0 on the FOMC bar itself). ann = close[j]/close[j-1] - 1 (the FOMC session's return). If 0 <= k < 15: return 1 if ann > 0, -1 if ann < 0, else 0. Otherwise 0.
rationale: Brooks, Katz and Lustig document that Treasury yields keep drifting in the direction of the FOMC-day change for several weeks after the announcement (a slow-moving-capital underreaction), so holding bonds in the announcement-day direction should earn the drift.
source: Brooks, Katz & Lustig 2018, 'Post-FOMC announcement drift in U.S. bond markets', NBER Working Paper 25127

name: Crypto intermediate-horizon reversal: long the 6 worst coins by their week-2-to-week-8 return, weekly (Jia-Goodell-Shen)
rule: rank() mode, rebalance weekly, universe CRYPTO_DAILY (18), eligible if bars > 60. EW crypto market = equal-weight mean of the daily returns of every eligible coin on each day (bars up to t only). Weights are equal 1/N over the chosen coins (N >= 3 else cash); sum <= 1. r_i = close[t-7]/close[t-56] - 1 (weeks 2 to 8, skipping the most recent week). Long the 6 lowest r_i, equal weight. Overseer fix: meta.warmup = 179 (3rd coin (LTC, 2017-12-13 = day 118) reaches 61 bars), so the deterministic cash warm-up is scored for neither the rule nor B&H.
rationale: Liu-Tsyvinski-Wu find crypto momentum only at 1-4 week horizons, and Jia, Goodell and Shen argue a reversal factor beats momentum as the third crypto factor; a skip-one-week, two-month reversal sort sits in the horizon where neither has been tested here.
source: Jia, Goodell & Shen 2022, 'Momentum or reversal: which is the appropriate third factor for cryptocurrencies?', Finance Research Letters 45, 102139; Liu, Tsyvinski & Wu 2022, JF 77(2)

name: Crypto frog-in-the-pan: among 12-week winners, long the 5 with the most continuous (least discrete) information arrival (Da-Gurun-Warachka transfer)
rule: rank() mode, rebalance weekly, universe CRYPTO_DAILY (18), eligible if bars > 95. EW crypto market = equal-weight mean of the daily returns of every eligible coin on each day (bars up to t only). Weights are equal 1/N over the chosen coins (N >= 3 else cash); sum <= 1. mom_i = close[t-7]/close[t-91] - 1. Over the 84 daily returns in the formation window (bars t-90..t-7): pctNeg = fraction of days with r < 0, pctPos = fraction with r > 0; ID_i = sign(mom_i) * (pctNeg - pctPos). Winners = the 9 highest mom_i (require mom_i > 0; fewer if fewer positive). Long the 5 winners with the lowest ID_i (most continuous), equal weight (min 3 else cash). Overseer fix: meta.warmup = 214 (3rd coin reaches 96 bars), so the deterministic cash warm-up is scored for neither the rule nor B&H.
rationale: Da, Gurun and Warachka show momentum is strongest when past returns arrived in many small steps (continuous information) because investors underreact to it; crypto is retail-dominated and attention-driven, so the frog-in-the-pan filter is a natural untested transfer.
source: Da, Gurun & Warachka 2014, 'Frog in the pan: continuous information and momentum', Review of Financial Studies 27(7), 2171-2218

name: Crypto pre-FOMC drift: long the 8 hourly coins from 19:00 UTC the day before an FOMC decision to 18:00 UTC on the decision day (Lucca-Moench; Pyo-Lee)
rule: signal() mode on 1h bars. hour(x) = floor(x/3600) % 24; ymd(x) = UTC date of epoch seconds x. FOMC decision dates = the FOMC_DATES list in research/hunt2/strategies/calendar-fomc-drift.mjs copied verbatim into the module (regular meetings 2016-01-27 .. 2025-03-19; the unscheduled 2020-03-03 and 2020-03-15 entries are excluded). n = bars[i].time + 3600 (the open of the bar the position will hold). Return 1 if (ymd(n) is the calendar day before an FOMC date and hour(n) >= 19) or (ymd(n) is an FOMC date and hour(n) < 18); else 0.
rationale: Lucca and Moench's pre-FOMC drift is a 24-hour run-up in risk assets before the 2pm ET statement with no post-announcement reversal; Pyo and Lee find bitcoin responds to FOMC events, so a 24/7 asset lets the exact pre-announcement window be isolated on hourly bars.
source: Lucca & Moench 2015, 'The pre-FOMC announcement drift', Journal of Finance 70(1), 329-371; Pyo & Lee 2020, 'Do FOMC and macroeconomic announcements affect Bitcoin prices?', Finance Research Letters 37, 101386

name: Crypto FOMC-cycle weeks: long all 18 coins in even FOMC-cycle weeks, flat in odd weeks (Cieslak-Morse-Vissing-Jorgensen transfer)
rule: signal() mode. Dates: ymd(t) = UTC calendar date of bar.time (epoch seconds; US bars open at 00:00 UTC of the session date); dow(t) = (floor(t/86400)+4) % 7 with 0 = Sunday. nextSession(t) = the next weekday date after ymd(t) (Fri -> Mon); a holiday error there only shifts a boundary by one session. FOMC decision dates = the FOMC_DATES list in research/hunt2/strategies/calendar-fomc-drift.mjs copied verbatim into the module (regular meetings 2016-01-27 .. 2025-03-19; the unscheduled 2020-03-03 and 2020-03-15 entries are excluded). Use the cycle-week definition of research/hunt2/strategies/r27-qqq-agg-fomc-cycle.mjs verbatim (D = the first weekday after ymd(t); week 0 if the next FOMC date is exactly one weekday after D, else k = weekdays from the previous FOMC date to D and week = k <= 3 ? 0 : 1 + floor((k-4)/5)). Return 1 if week is even, else 0. Bars before 2016-01-26 return 0.
rationale: Cieslak, Morse and Vissing-Jorgensen show the equity premium is earned in even weeks of the FOMC cycle, which they tie to informal Fed communication; if the channel is policy news rather than equity-specific flows, a Fed-sensitive risk asset like crypto should show the same parity.
source: Cieslak, Morse & Vissing-Jorgensen 2019, 'Stock returns over the FOMC cycle', Journal of Finance 74(5), 2201-2248

name: Crypto intermediate momentum echo: long the top 6 by the week-5-to-week-12 return, weekly (Novy-Marx transfer)
rule: rank() mode, rebalance weekly, universe CRYPTO_DAILY (18), eligible if bars > 90. EW crypto market = equal-weight mean of the daily returns of every eligible coin on each day (bars up to t only). Weights are equal 1/N over the chosen coins (N >= 3 else cash); sum <= 1. r_i = close[t-28]/close[t-84] - 1 (weeks 5 to 12, skipping the most recent 4 weeks). Long the 6 highest r_i, equal weight. Overseer fix: meta.warmup = 209 (3rd coin reaches 91 bars), so the deterministic cash warm-up is scored for neither the rule nor B&H.
rationale: Novy-Marx finds the intermediate past (months 12-7) drives equity momentum more than the recent past; crypto momentum has only been tested at 1-4 week and 3-month horizons here, so the 'echo' window with the recent month removed is an untested horizon.
source: Novy-Marx 2012, 'Is momentum really momentum?', Journal of Financial Economics 103(3), 429-453

name: Crypto downside beta: long the 6 coins with the highest beta to the crypto market on its down days, weekly (Zhang-Li-Xiong-Wang)
rule: rank() mode, rebalance weekly, universe CRYPTO_DAILY (18), eligible if bars > 185. EW crypto market = equal-weight mean of the daily returns of every eligible coin on each day (bars up to t only). Weights are equal 1/N over the chosen coins (N >= 3 else cash); sum <= 1. Over the last 180 sessions with m = EW crypto market return: D = days with m < mean(m over the window). betaDown_i = cov(r_i, m over D) / var(m over D) (at least 40 days in D else cash). Long the 6 highest betaDown_i, equal weight. Overseer fix: meta.warmup = 303 (3rd coin reaches 186 bars), so the deterministic cash warm-up is scored for neither the rule nor B&H.
rationale: Zhang, Li, Xiong and Wang document a positive downside-beta premium in the cryptocurrency cross-section that survives controls for market beta, size and momentum, consistent with investors demanding compensation for coins that fall hardest in crypto sell-offs.
source: Zhang, Li, Xiong & Wang 2021, 'Downside risk and the cross-section of cryptocurrency returns', Journal of Banking & Finance 133, 106246; Ang, Chen & Xing 2006, RFS 19(4)

name: Crypto high idiosyncratic volatility: long the 6 coins with the highest residual volatility to the crypto market, weekly (Zhang-Li)
rule: rank() mode, rebalance weekly, universe CRYPTO_DAILY (18), eligible if bars > 35. EW crypto market = equal-weight mean of the daily returns of every eligible coin on each day (bars up to t only). Weights are equal 1/N over the chosen coins (N >= 3 else cash); sum <= 1. Over the last 30 sessions regress r_i on the EW crypto market m (OLS with intercept); ivol_i = sample std of the residuals. Long the 6 highest ivol_i, equal weight. Overseer fix: meta.warmup = 154 (3rd coin reaches 36 bars), so the deterministic cash warm-up is scored for neither the rule nor B&H.
rationale: Zhang and Li report a positive idiosyncratic-volatility premium in crypto (the opposite sign to the Ang et al. equity puzzle), consistent with under-diversified holders being paid for coin-specific risk; the prior test here used total volatility and the low leg only.
source: Zhang & Li 2020, 'Is idiosyncratic volatility priced in cryptocurrency markets?', Physica A 553, 124125; Ang, Hodrick, Xing & Zhang 2006, JF 61(1)

name: Crypto salience: long the 6 coins with the lowest salience-weighted past-3-week return, weekly (Cosemans-Frehen transfer)
rule: rank() mode, rebalance weekly, universe CRYPTO_DAILY (18), eligible if bars > 25. EW crypto market = equal-weight mean of the daily returns of every eligible coin on each day (bars up to t only). Weights are equal 1/N over the chosen coins (N >= 3 else cash); sum <= 1. Over the last 21 sessions (bars t-20..t): rbar_d = EW crypto market return on day d; sal_i,d = |r_i,d - rbar_d| / (|r_i,d| + |rbar_d| + 0.1). For each name rank its 21 days by sal descending (k = 1 most salient); omega_k = 0.7^k / sum_{j=1..21} 0.7^j. ST_i = sum_d (omega_i,d - 1/21) * r_i,d (covariance between the salience weight and the return). Long the 6 lowest ST_i, equal weight. (Variant of c1023-acad2-05 on the crypto cross-section.) Overseer fix: meta.warmup = 144 (3rd coin reaches 26 bars), so the deterministic cash warm-up is scored for neither the rule nor B&H.
rationale: Crypto investors are retail-heavy and attention-driven, the population salience theory describes best; if salient upside moves get over-bought, coins with the lowest salience-weighted recent returns should outperform.
source: Cosemans & Frehen 2021, 'Salience theory and stock prices: empirical evidence', Journal of Financial Economics 140(2), 460-483; Bordalo, Gennaioli & Shleifer 2012, QJE 127(3)

name: Crypto same-weekday seasonality: each day long the 6 coins with the best average return on the coming weekday over the past year (Keloharju-Linnainmaa-Nyberg transfer)
rule: rank() mode, rebalance daily, universe CRYPTO_DAILY (18), eligible if bars > 370. EW crypto market = equal-weight mean of the daily returns of every eligible coin on each day (bars up to t only). Weights are equal 1/N over the chosen coins (N >= 3 else cash); sum <= 1. Dates: ymd(t) = UTC calendar date of bar.time (epoch seconds; US bars open at 00:00 UTC of the session date); dow(t) = (floor(t/86400)+4) % 7 with 0 = Sunday. nextSession(t) = the next weekday date after ymd(t) (Fri -> Mon); a holiday error there only shifts a boundary by one session. W = dow(bars[i].time + 86400) (the UTC weekday of the day the position holds, 0-6, crypto trades every day). score_i = mean of r_i over the 52 past sessions in bars t-363..t whose dow equals W. Long the 6 highest score_i, equal weight. Overseer fix: meta.warmup = 488 (3rd coin reaches 371 bars), so the deterministic cash warm-up is scored for neither the rule nor B&H.
rationale: Keloharju, Linnainmaa and Nyberg find cross-sectional return seasonalities at the weekday frequency, with the same names repeatedly doing well on the same weekday; crypto's 7-day week and known weekend/Sunday effects make the cross-sectional version a natural untested transfer.
source: Keloharju, Linnainmaa & Nyberg 2016, 'Return seasonalities', Journal of Finance 71(4), 1557-1590; Kaiser 2019, Finance Research Letters 31

name: Crypto pre-holiday drift: long all 18 coins over the UTC day before each NYSE holiday (Ariel transfer; Qadan-Aharon-Eichel)
rule: signal() mode. Dates: ymd(t) = UTC calendar date of bar.time (epoch seconds; US bars open at 00:00 UTC of the session date); dow(t) = (floor(t/86400)+4) % 7 with 0 = Sunday. nextSession(t) = the next weekday date after ymd(t) (Fri -> Mon); a holiday error there only shifts a boundary by one session. NYSE holidays (deterministic rules, observed on the nearest weekday when on a weekend): Jan 1; 3rd Monday Jan; 3rd Monday Feb; Good Friday (Easter via the Gregorian computus); last Monday May; Jun 19 (from 2022); Jul 4; 1st Monday Sep; 4th Thursday Nov; Dec 25. D = ymd(bars[i].time + 86400) (the UTC day the position holds). Return 1 if D is a weekday that is not itself a holiday and the first weekday after D is an NYSE holiday (D is the US pre-holiday session); else 0.
rationale: The pre-holiday drift is one of the oldest equity calendar effects and crypto now co-moves with US risk appetite and US trading hours; Qadan, Aharon and Eichel document US-calendar effects in crypto, so the pre-holiday session is a cheap, untested transfer.
source: Ariel 1990, 'High stock returns before holidays', Journal of Finance 45(5); Qadan, Aharon & Eichel 2022, 'Seasonal and calendar effects and the price efficiency of cryptocurrencies', Finance Research Letters 46, 102354

name: Crypto momentum gap: 3-week momentum top 6 only when the winner-loser spread is below its historical median, weekly (Huang transfer)
rule: rank() mode, rebalance weekly, universe CRYPTO_DAILY (18), eligible if bars > 25. EW crypto market = equal-weight mean of the daily returns of every eligible coin on each day (bars up to t only). Weights are equal 1/N over the chosen coins (N >= 3 else cash); sum <= 1. mom_i = close[t]/close[t-21] - 1. gap_t = (90th percentile of mom) - (10th percentile of mom) across eligible coins. Keep ctx.state.gaps = every gap_t from earlier weekly rebalances (expanding, excluding t). If fewer than 26 entries: cash (still push). Else if gap_t <= median(ctx.state.gaps): long the 6 highest mom_i, equal weight; else cash. Push gap_t after deciding. (Variant of c1023-acad2-01 on the crypto cross-section.) Overseer fix: percentiles use linear interpolation on the sorted cross-section; gap_t is computed (and pushed) only when at least 3 coins are eligible, else cash without a push. Overseer fix: meta.warmup = 335 (3rd coin eligible (day 143) plus 26 weekly gap observations), so the deterministic cash warm-up is scored for neither the rule nor B&H.
rationale: Crypto momentum crashes are frequent and violent; Huang's momentum gap predicts that the premium is low after formation periods with a wide winner-loser spread, so the gap should be an a-priori crash filter for the 3-week crypto momentum that round 1 found fragile.
source: Huang 2022, 'The momentum gap and return predictability', Journal of Financial Economics 143(1), 42-62; Liu, Tsyvinski & Wu 2022, JF 77(2)

name: Crypto crash sensitivity to Bitcoin: long the 6 alts with the highest lower-tail dependence with BTC, weekly (Chabi-Yo-Ruenzi-Weigert transfer)
rule: rank() mode, rebalance weekly, universe CRYPTO_DAILY (18), eligible if bars > 370. EW crypto market = equal-weight mean of the daily returns of every eligible coin on each day (bars up to t only). Weights are equal 1/N over the chosen coins (N >= 3 else cash); sum <= 1. Over the last 365 sessions: q_i = the 5th percentile of r_i, q_m = the 5th percentile of the BTCUSDT daily return m (both over the same window, linear interpolation). LTD_i = (# days with r_i <= q_i AND m <= q_m) / (# days with m <= q_m). Names whose window is incomplete are ineligible. BTCUSDT itself is never picked. Long the 6 highest LTD_i among the other coins, equal weight. (Variant of c1023-acad2-03 with BTC as the market.) Overseer fix: meta.warmup = 613 (BTC plus 3 alts (4th coin ADA, day 243) reach 371 bars), so the deterministic cash warm-up is scored for neither the rule nor B&H.
rationale: Alt-coins that collapse exactly on Bitcoin's worst days are the crypto analogue of crash-sensitive stocks; if the crash-sensitivity premium is a general risk compensation it should show up against the BTC tail in a cross-section where tail events are frequent enough to measure.
source: Chabi-Yo, Ruenzi & Weigert 2018, 'Crash sensitivity and the cross-section of expected stock returns', JFQA 53(3), 1059-1100

name: Crypto prospect-theory value: long the 6 coins with the lowest TK value of the past 52 weekly returns, weekly (Barberis-Mukherjee-Wang transfer)
rule: rank() mode, rebalance weekly, universe CRYPTO_DAILY (18), eligible if bars > 30. EW crypto market = equal-weight mean of the daily returns of every eligible coin on each day (bars up to t only). Weights are equal 1/N over the chosen coins (N >= 3 else cash); sum <= 1. Weekly returns from ctx.resample(universe[sym], '1w') using only complete weeks; eligible only with at least 52 complete weeks, and the last 52 are used (L = 52). TK of a return list of length L: v(x) = x^0.88 for x >= 0 and -2.25*(-x)^0.88 for x < 0; w+(p) = p^0.61/(p^0.61+(1-p)^0.61)^(1/0.61); w-(p) = p^0.69/(p^0.69+(1-p)^0.69)^(1/0.69). Sort the m negative returns ascending r(-m) <= ... <= r(-1) and the n non-negative returns ascending r(1) <= ... <= r(n). TK = sum_{j=1..m} v(r(-j)) * [w-(j/L) - w-((j-1)/L)] + sum_{j=1..n} v(r(j)) * [w+((n-j+1)/L) - w+((n-j)/L)]. Long the 6 lowest TK, equal weight. (Variant of c1023-acad2-10 with weekly returns.) Overseer fix: meta.warmup = 495 (3rd coin has 52 complete weeks), so the deterministic cash warm-up is scored for neither the rule nor B&H.
rationale: Crypto's lottery-like return distributions are where prospect-theory overpricing of positively skewed, big-past-gain assets should bite hardest; the TK sort has not been run on a crypto cross-section here.
source: Barberis, Mukherjee & Wang 2016, 'Prospect theory and stock returns: an empirical test', Review of Financial Studies 29(11), 3068-3107

name: Crypto low volatility-of-volatility: long the 6 coins whose rolling 7-day volatility was most stable over 60 days, weekly (Baltussen-van Bekkum-van der Grient transfer)
rule: rank() mode, rebalance weekly, universe CRYPTO_DAILY (18), eligible if bars > 70. EW crypto market = equal-weight mean of the daily returns of every eligible coin on each day (bars up to t only). Weights are equal 1/N over the chosen coins (N >= 3 else cash); sum <= 1. v_d = sample std of the 7 daily returns ending on day d (via ctx.rollingStd('ret', 7, d)). Over the last 60 sessions, volOfVol_i = std(v_d) / mean(v_d) (coefficient of variation of the rolling vol). Long the 6 lowest volOfVol_i, equal weight. Overseer fix: ctx.rollingStd does not exist in rank() mode; compute v_d directly as the sample std (n-1) of the 7 daily close-to-close returns ending on day d from universe bars up to t. Overseer fix: meta.warmup = 189 (3rd coin reaches 71 bars), so the deterministic cash warm-up is scored for neither the rule nor B&H.
rationale: Baltussen, van Bekkum and van der Grient find assets with uncertain risk (high vol-of-vol) earn low returns because investors with ambiguity aversion avoid them; crypto volatility is both high and highly time-varying, and the stock-only test here was never transferred.
source: Baltussen, van Bekkum & van der Grient 2018, 'Unknown unknowns: uncertainty about risk and stock returns', Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis 53(4), 1615-1651
